problem_text:
A regional courier network must dispatch a single vehicle to service seven distinct distribution hubs, each positioned at specific geographical points on a grid:
Hub Alpha: Coordinates (121,101)
Hub Beta: Coordinates (160,20)
Hub Gamma: Coordinates (5,70)
Hub Delta: Coordinates (115,29)
Hub Epsilon: Coordinates (65,34)
Hub Zeta: Coordinates (167,133)
Hub Eta: Coordinates (166,165)

The travel distances, in kilometers, along available direct corridors are as follows:
Alpha to Gamma: 120.1 km
Alpha to Delta: 72.2 km
Alpha to Epsilon: 87.3 km
Alpha to Zeta: 56.0 km
Alpha to Eta: 78.2 km
Beta to Gamma: 162.9 km
Beta to Delta: 45.9 km
Beta to Epsilon: 96.0 km
Beta to Zeta: 113.2 km
Beta to Eta: 145.1 km
Gamma to Delta: 117.4 km
Gamma to Epsilon: 70.0 km
Gamma to Zeta: 173.8 km
Gamma to Eta: 186.9 km
Delta to Epsilon: 50.2 km
Delta to Zeta: 116.3 km
Delta to Eta: 145.2 km
Epsilon to Zeta: 142.1 km
Epsilon to Eta: 165.4 km
Zeta to Eta: 32.0 km

Due to regulatory restrictions, a direct connection between Hub Alpha and Hub Beta is prohibited. Furthermore, the route planning must incorporate a mandatory selection rule: exactly one of the two critical links—either the corridor connecting Beta and Gamma or the corridor connecting Gamma and Delta—must be part of the final circuit.

The objective is to determine the minimal total travel distance for a closed loop that visits every hub precisely once before returning to the origin point.
